paper_title: Explainable multimodal deep learning for predicting thyroid
concern_text: DCA assumes all true AI predictions are beneficial — not true for microscopic metastases. Proposed workflow would not be best clinical management.
author_response: Revised DCA accounting for clinically insignificant metastases.

paper_title: Explainable multimodal deep learning for predicting thyroid
concern_text: Comparison with human experts unfair due to differing dataset sizes (model on full data vs radiologists on N=200).
author_response: Added model performance on same N=200 subset.

paper_title: Explainable multimodal deep learning for predicting thyroid
concern_text: LLNM-Net trained on cancerous nodules only — most thyroid nodules are benign. Cannot be used for population screening.
author_response: Clarified intended use is pre-surgical planning, not screening.

paper_title: Medical multimodal multitask foundation model for lung cance
concern_text: CVD mortality as binary label is over-simplification — it is right-censored time-to-event data. Should stratify by cut-off years like cancer risk task.
author_response: Added time-stratified CVD analysis.

paper_title: Medical multimodal multitask foundation model for lung cance
concern_text: Clinical metadata encoded as predefined-rule text — fundamentally differs from natural language. Is this necessary vs simply encoding as array?
author_response: Added ablation comparing text vs tabular encoding.

paper_title: Medical multimodal multitask foundation model for lung cance
concern_text: AUC improvements for MT-MM are small in some cases. Need critical perspective balancing gains vs extra effort.
author_response: Added cost analysis and honest discussion of marginal gains.

paper_title: Medical multimodal multitask foundation model for lung cance
concern_text: Heatmaps show apparently useless tokens ('brother', '142') as important. Can multi-source information be shown to be composed in complementary way?
author_response: Added token-level attribution analysis.

paper_title: Multimodal histopathologic models stratify hormone receptor-
concern_text: Correlation of 0.6 does not indicate reliable individual prediction. No individual-level performance data vs gold-standard. Need calibration plot with censoring.
author_response: Added individual-level analysis and calibration plots.

paper_title: Multimodal histopathologic models stratify hormone receptor-
concern_text: Cut-off in Orpheus for high-risk classification not specified. Does it vary across populations?
author_response: Reported cut-off with cross-cohort sensitivity analysis.

paper_title: Multimodal histopathologic models stratify hormone receptor-
concern_text: Claim that Orpheus enhances beyond Oncotype DX needs tempering — linear models developed within Oncotype risk groups, comparison may not be equitable.
author_response: Tempered claims and added independent evaluation.

paper_title: Quantifying portable genetic effects and improving cross-anc
concern_text: Type I error simulations only 100 times — not enough at 0.05 level. Need ≥1,000. Also need FDR threshold sensitivity analysis.
author_response: Increased to 1,000 simulations with FDR sensitivity.

paper_title: Quantifying portable genetic effects and improving cross-anc
concern_text: Only simulated on chromosome 22 — heritability disproportionally large, samples highly related. Need whole-genome simulation.
author_response: Added whole-genome simulations.

paper_title: Quantifying portable genetic effects and improving cross-anc
concern_text: Only East Asian and European. Transferability to African samples is harder. Should apply to AFR samples.
author_response: Added African ancestry analysis using PAGE.

paper_title: Quantifying portable genetic effects and improving cross-anc
concern_text: X-Wing only marginally better than PRS-CSx. Need scenario simulations showing when each method wins.
author_response: Added scenario-based simulations.

paper_title: Development and external validation of prediction algorithms
concern_text: Time horizon for prediction not found — paramount importance. Are models predicting imminent diagnoses or long-term risk? Models with very high AUC may just be diagnosing established cancers.
author_response: Clarified 2-year window and added time-stratified analyses.

paper_title: Development and external validation of prediction algorithms
concern_text: Fundamental difference between predicting probability cancer is already present vs probability of developing cancer in the future. These concepts are conflated.
author_response: Revised terminology: 'risk of cancer diagnosis' instead of 'cancer risk'.

paper_title: Development and external validation of prediction algorithms
concern_text: Missing data shown not to be MCAR. Imputation method doesn't handle MNAR. Need reporting of N missing and bias analysis.
author_response: Added MNAR sensitivity analysis.

paper_title: Development and external validation of prediction algorithms
concern_text: Variables kept based on P values. Did you consider data-driven variable selection?
author_response: Added LASSO comparison showing similar results.

paper_title: Development and external validation of prediction algorithms
concern_text: Calibration intercept/slope should be in main text. Blood tests add almost nothing — discuss clinical implications.
author_response: Added calibration to main text, discussed limited value of blood tests.

paper_title: Development and external validation of prediction algorithms
concern_text: DCA not commonly used — need explanation. Cancer-specific DCA needed, aggregate 'any cancer' DCA makes little sense.
author_response: Added cancer-specific DCA with interpretation.

paper_title: Development and external validation of prediction algorithms
concern_text: Model coefficients and variables need to be clearly provided to allow further validation.
author_response: Provided full coefficients in supplementary tables.

paper_title: A noninvasive model for chronic kidney disease screening and
concern_text: Sample size lacks formal power calculations and has concerning issues in key subgroups like Somalia cohort (n=47) and less common pathological types like MCD/FSGS. This raises questions about statistical power.
author_response: We added power calculations and explicitly stated limited power for rare subtypes. Somalia cohort results reported with appropriate caveats.

paper_title: A noninvasive model for chronic kidney disease screening and
concern_text: Missing data handling lacks adequate documentation — no clear explanation of how missing values were managed, no reporting of missing data percentages, no sensitivity analyses to assess impact.
author_response: We added missing data reporting, imputation methodology, and sensitivity analysis.

paper_title: A noninvasive model for chronic kidney disease screening and
concern_text: Model calibration is insufficiently reported — calibration plots relegated to supplementary materials, no formal calibration testing (such as Hosmer-Lemeshow) presented.
author_response: We moved calibration plots to main figures and added Hosmer-Lemeshow test results.

paper_title: A noninvasive model for chronic kidney disease screening and
concern_text: Multiple testing concerns remain unaddressed — no clear adjustment for multiple comparisons across numerous statistical tests performed.
author_response: We added Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons and flagged results that do not survive correction.

paper_title: A noninvasive model for chronic kidney disease screening and
concern_text: The authors categorize MCD or FSGS as combined feature. It is reasonable to combine primary MCD/FSGS as podocytopathies, but secondary FSGS is much more frequent and has different clinical management.
author_response: We discussed the MCD/FSGS distinction and added sensitivity analysis separating primary vs secondary FSGS.

paper_title: A noninvasive model for chronic kidney disease screening and
concern_text: The Net Reclassification Index (NRI) has well-documented issues with the category-free version and should be interpreted with caution. The term 'metadata' is confusing — it relates to actual clinical data, not metadata.
author_response: We clarified NRI limitations and changed 'metadata' to 'clinical data' throughout.

paper_title: Prehospital real-time AI for trauma mortality prediction: a
concern_text: The model was developed and internally validated in South Korean trauma centers. External validation in Australia (n=3,578) is valuable but limited to one center. Performance in other healthcare systems (e.g., US, European EMS) would strengthen generalizability claims.
author_response: We acknowledged geographic limitation and discussed plans for broader international validation. Added sensitivity analysis by injury mechanism.

paper_title: Prehospital real-time AI for trauma mortality prediction: a
concern_text: Calibration analysis should be presented more prominently. The model's predicted probabilities vs observed mortality rates should be clearly shown across risk groups.
author_response: We moved calibration plots to main figures and added calibration metrics (slope, intercept, Brier score).

paper_title: Prehospital real-time AI for trauma mortality prediction: a
concern_text: How would this model be deployed in real-time prehospital settings? What are the latency requirements? What happens when data is missing (common in trauma settings)?
author_response: We described the real-time deployment architecture, measured inference latency (<1s), and added analysis of model robustness to missing prehospital variables.

paper_title: Prehospital real-time AI for trauma mortality prediction: a
concern_text: The study follows TRIPOD+AI and TRIPOD-cluster guidelines — this is commendable. Minor formatting improvements needed in checklist compliance table.
author_response: We reformatted the TRIPOD+AI checklist table.

paper_title: Machine learning models identify predictive features of pati
concern_text: Authors should provide rationale why selecting XGBoost, not other ML models. Unclear whether further feature selection can improve performance.
author_response: Added comparison with RF, LR, SVM. XGBoost selected for best AUC and interpretability via TreeSHAP.

paper_title: Machine learning models identify predictive features of pati
concern_text: Class imbalance is a major issue — subjects at later stages naturally have higher mortality. Difference between 1-year and 10-year models may simply reflect class imbalance rather than genuine finding. Need class-balanced resampling or class-weighted loss.
author_response: Added class-weighted analysis and SMOTE sensitivity analysis. Results robust to rebalancing.

paper_title: Machine learning models identify predictive features of pati
concern_text: Missing result figures. Discussion mentions survival analysis differed across dementia types but corresponding figures cannot be found in manuscript or supplementary material.
author_response: Added missing survival curves by dementia subtype.

paper_title: Machine learning models identify predictive features of pati
concern_text: Model performance evaluated only with AUC. Additional metrics like sensitivity, specificity, F1, and calibration should be reported for clinical applicability.
author_response: Added full metric panel including sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, F1.

paper_title: Machine learning models identify predictive features of pati
concern_text: Whether adding genetic or multi-omics data may improve prediction further in future studies should be discussed.
author_response: Added discussion of potential for genomic/proteomic data integration.

paper_title: An interpretable machine learning algorithm enables dynamic
concern_text: The study lacks external validation. Model should be tested in very different conditions to avoid out-of-distribution bias.
author_response: Acknowledged as limitation and discussed plans for multi-center validation.

paper_title: An interpretable machine learning algorithm enables dynamic
concern_text: Why LightGBM as first choice? There are many time-series models like LSTM that may better capture temporal patterns. Also, SOFA score uses much less variables — for parsimony, SOFA seems better for practical use.
author_response: Compared with LSTM and showed LightGBM competitive. SOFA comparison added showing ML model significantly outperforms.

paper_title: An interpretable machine learning algorithm enables dynamic
concern_text: The outcome variable is imbalanced data. What is the proportion of deceased during the time frame?
author_response: Added mortality proportion and class imbalance handling discussion.

paper_title: An interpretable machine learning algorithm enables dynamic
concern_text: Will stacked ensemble model further improve performance? There is evidence that ensemble models achieve better accuracy than any individual model alone.
author_response: Discussed ensemble potential in future directions.

paper_title: An interpretable machine learning algorithm enables dynamic
concern_text: Why update every 24 hours to predict 48-hour mortality, rather than every hour or every 6/12 hours for shorter horizons? Need clear rationale for this design choice.
author_response: Added clinical rationale: 24h update aligns with ICU rounding schedules and clinical decision cycles.

paper_title: An interpretable machine learning algorithm enables dynamic
concern_text: PPV remains low indicating many false alarms. How to interpret or handle these false alarms?
author_response: Added false alarm analysis with risk stratification tiers to reduce alarm fatigue.

paper_title: An interpretable machine learning algorithm enables dynamic
concern_text: While model accuracy is important, it may not translate to clinical benefits such as reducing mortality in ICU. More work needed to test effectiveness.
author_response: Added discussion of implementation pathway and need for prospective impact study.

paper_title: Machine learning for early dynamic prediction of functional
concern_text: Most literature uses discharge data for 3-month outcomes, or uses time-varying data for in-hospital outcomes. Using 72h data to predict 3-month outcome — by the time prediction is made, patient status will change many times. Median LOS is 7-10 days for ischemic stroke. The 72h prediction becomes irrelevant. Authors should either predict at discharge, or predict in-hospital outcomes.
author_response: Added analysis at discharge timepoint and discussed clinical decision points where 72h prediction is relevant (early transfer decisions).

paper_title: Machine learning for early dynamic prediction of functional
concern_text: Significant risk of cherry-picking models when there is no bootstrapping with multiple random splits. While authors bootstrap the CV procedure, they need equivalent process for training/testing split with confidence intervals around AUC, accuracy, specificity.
author_response: Added 100-repetition bootstrapped train/test splits with CI for all metrics.

paper_title: Machine learning for early dynamic prediction of functional
concern_text: The fact that some patients were associated with multiple admissions might positively bias the performance of the model. Recommend including only the first admission per patient.
author_response: Added sensitivity analysis with first-admission-only and showed consistent results.

paper_title: Machine learning for early dynamic prediction of functional
concern_text: XGBoost has equivalent or better performance compared to transformer. XGBoost doesn't incorporate varying time-series. Why should clinicians prefer a more complex model that is harder to implement?
author_response: Added complexity-performance trade-off analysis. Recommended XGBoost for practical deployment.

paper_title: Machine learning for early dynamic prediction of functional
concern_text: ICD codes are notoriously inaccurate — over 30% of patients in claims with acute ischemic stroke did not actually have the condition. Recommend independent audit of random sample.
author_response: Added chart review validation of 200 random patients confirming >95% accuracy of ICD coding.

paper_title: Machine learning for early dynamic prediction of functional
concern_text: The study period involves initial phases of COVID-19. Do models account for whether a patient's stroke was provoked by COVID-19?
author_response: Added COVID-19 status as covariate in sensitivity analysis.

paper_title: Methodological choices and clinical usefulness for machine l
concern_text: 67% accuracy defined as benchmark for clinical usefulness. Unclear why a 33% error rate should be good enough for clinical practice. Base rate of the binary variable (50% symptom reduction yes/no) should be reported to evaluate prediction quality.
author_response: Added base rate reporting and clinical justification for the 67% threshold based on existing literature.

paper_title: Methodological choices and clinical usefulness for machine l
concern_text: Introduction seems superficial and does not consider relevant literature on predictive models in psychotherapy research, especially for binary outcomes. Comparable recent papers in dropout prediction not cited.
author_response: Expanded introduction with relevant psychotherapy prediction literature.

paper_title: Methodological choices and clinical usefulness for machine l
concern_text: Unconvinced by multiple imputation of outcomes. Potential risk of introducing label noise. Authors should discuss this in the discussion.
author_response: Added discussion of imputation risks. Results presented both with and without outcome imputation.

paper_title: Methodological choices and clinical usefulness for machine l
concern_text: Great that ML pipeline is available, but code is hard to read from a PDF. Please upload to GitHub.
author_response: Code uploaded to GitHub repository.

paper_title: AI-guided patient stratification improves outcomes and effic
concern_text: Results are not very impressive — mainly the difference between sensitivity and specificity. Existing approaches show much better performance up to 97% accuracy. Technical contributions are limited.
author_response: Clarified that the novelty is cross-dataset generalization (ADNI→AMARANTH without retraining), not raw accuracy. Added context for existing methods.

paper_title: AI-guided patient stratification improves outcomes and effic
concern_text: The most critical element — that the model was trained on ADNI and applied to AMARANTH without retraining — is not sufficiently emphasised. This represents the key contribution and should be made clear earlier.
author_response: Restructured introduction and abstract to emphasize cross-dataset generalization upfront.

paper_title: AI-guided patient stratification improves outcomes and effic
concern_text: Since the true treatment effect in clinical trials is inherently unknown, further discussion of what evidence supports the model's consistency across datasets would strengthen the manuscript.
author_response: Added discussion of external consistency evidence and limitations of post-hoc trial analysis.

paper_title: AI-guided patient stratification improves outcomes and effic
concern_text: Figures need axes labels and units. The outcomes and methodology are not reflecting the claim of interpretable AI model.
author_response: Improved all figure labels and added interpretability analysis section.

paper_title: Multimodal deep learning for Alzheimer's disease dementia as
concern_text: GPs usually do not have access to MRI scanner — one of the most important features is MRI-based. For clinical trials, biomarker evidence for amyloid pathology would be preferred but is not included.
author_response: Added analysis of model performance without MRI and discussed deployment scenarios.

paper_title: Multimodal deep learning for Alzheimer's disease dementia as
concern_text: Model trained on clinical diagnosis — up to 30% of individuals with clinical AD dementia do not have AD pathology. Comparison with clinicians reflects differences between new vs old clinicians, not model superiority. Also APOE is missing for non-AD cohorts — presence of APOE alone could predict AD vs non-AD almost perfectly.
author_response: Added neuropathological validation subset and discussed diagnostic label noise. APOE missingness handled with explicit analysis.

paper_title: Multimodal deep learning for Alzheimer's disease dementia as
concern_text: Dementia vs non-dementia classification is trivial — diagnosis determined based on neuropsych test scores and MMSE, so it's circular that these features predict the diagnosis perfectly. The harder and more relevant task is AD vs non-AD dementias.
author_response: Added focused analysis on AD vs non-AD subtypes and discussed the circular nature of the dementia vs non-dementia classification.

paper_title: Multimodal deep learning for Alzheimer's disease dementia as
concern_text: How were MRI scans harmonised across cohorts? How were cohort-specific missing data dealt with? APOE is missing in entire Parkinson and FTD cohorts — this creates a confound.
author_response: Added MRI harmonization details and missing data handling methodology.

paper_title: Multimodal deep learning for Alzheimer's disease dementia as
concern_text: Unclear how external validation dataset was chosen. Manuscript mentions splitting into folds but explanation vague. How are AUC and other metrics independent of tuning and training?
author_response: Clarified validation strategy with explicit held-out external datasets.

paper_title: AI-driven fusion of multimodal data for Alzheimer's disease
concern_text: AUROC of 0.79/0.84 for amyloid/tau classification — should report calibration and net benefit analysis. Without these, clinical applicability cannot be assessed.
author_response: Added calibration plots and DCA analysis.

paper_title: AI-driven fusion of multimodal data for Alzheimer's disease
concern_text: Seven cohorts used but unclear how independent the external validation truly is. Need clear delineation of which cohorts used for development vs validation.
author_response: Restructured to clearly separate 4 development cohorts from 3 validation cohorts.

paper_title: AI-driven fusion of multimodal data for Alzheimer's disease
concern_text: The clinical utility depends on whether this replaces PET scanning. How does the model perform in the specific clinical scenario where PET is being considered but not yet obtained?
author_response: Added analysis of model as PET pre-screening tool with cost-effectiveness comparison.
